A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAE/CAE+ research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison across the substantial reformatting and relocation of content.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo and MiniHack experiments, including comparative results in Tables 3–5 and ablations and learning curves in the main text and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and adds Habitat experiments, trajectory comparisons, and MiniHack runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The critic-embedding bonuses and CAE+ inverse-dynamics architecture remain. However, Algorithm 1 changes the running-statistics recurrence and normalization, and Algorithm 3 corrects the gradient-update sign and includes discounting. Section 3.2 also adds embedding/action concatenation as an alternative input construction. These are limited revisions to the written procedures; they do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v2 adds reward-free exploration on Habitat using HM3D indoor environments and PointNav, including evaluation in unseen scenes. This substantially extends coverage beyond dense-reward MuJoCo and sparse-reward MiniHack. The MuJoCo tasks and nine explicitly reported MiniHack tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Reported comparisons retain PPO, TD3, SAC, and DSAC on MuJoCo and E3B on MiniHack. Habitat extends the existing E3B/CAE/CAE+ comparison set. Despite expanded baseline wording, ICM, RND, RIDE, and NovelD results remain attributed to E3B papers; BDQN appears only in the related-work comparison.

E3.justification: The new Habitat protocol trains PPO with intrinsic bonuses for 100 million interaction steps and evaluates the proportion of unseen environments revealed. Appendix E.3 specifies disabled bonus scaling and three inverse-dynamics updates per PPO epoch. Separately, the reported MiniHack U dimension changes from 256 to '128 or 256'; task assignments and whether retained experiments were rerun are unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 adds a MiniHack wall-clock efficiency comparison and a Habitat trajectory case study in Figure 3. The existing scaling and transformation-U ablations remain, with identical plotted curves; moving the scaling ablation into Appendix E does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: The retained experiments use the same five MuJoCo seeds and three MiniHack seeds, with the same plus/minus reporting and shaded curves. Habitat follows the existing three-seed reporting practice. Revised N6 uncertainty values are result changes, with no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing reported.

E6.justification: New Habitat results report CAE+ 0.69 ± 0.074, E3B 0.51 ± 0.097, and CAE 0.49 ± 0.102; MiniHack runtimes are approximately 17 hours for CAE versus 22 for E3B. In Table 5, N6 E3B changes from 0.77 ± 0.041 to 0.75 ± 0.019, CAE from -0.45 ± 0.222 to -0.46 ± 0.193, and CAE+ from 0.94 ± 0.016 to 0.94 ± 0.014. N6 RPI changes from 22.08% to 25.3%. MuJoCo scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 substantively revises the central regret analysis: it changes logarithmic factors in the bounds, corrects signs in the stochastic-error definitions, and replaces maximum-based failure-probability combinations with union-bound allocations. Appendix D.1 adds a uniform-convergence argument sketch for dependence that v1 explicitly left unaddressed. The input-normalization and positive-kernel assumptions already existed in v1's appendix; their relocation alone is not new theory.

C1.justification: The principal contributions—reusing critic embeddings, lightweight CAE+, and sublinear-regret guarantees—remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the claimed empirical applicability and effectiveness to Habitat and reward-free environments.

C2.justification: v2 explains how inverse-dynamics learning constrains shared embeddings, adds discussion defending the theoretical assumptions, and explicitly acknowledges non-negligible matrix-inversion overhead in Appendix F. It also makes explicit superiority inferences over ICM, RND, RIDE, and NovelD based on outperforming E3B, without presenting those methods' results.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation expands through a project-code link, explicit upstream-code URLs, OS/CPU/GPU specifications, training-time information, and Habitat hyperparameter Tables 11–12. Appendix A also revises the CAE+ implementation snippet, including default-action inputs already described in v1's method. These disclosures do not establish changes to the implementations used for retained results.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of potential-based reward shaping, Liberty, EME, BDQN, and additional provable-exploration work, alongside Habitat/HM3D references. This qualifies the contrast between heuristic and theoretically grounded exploration while retaining the original neural-bandit positioning.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively revised across the introduction, related work, methodology, and theoretical discussion. Related work is reorganized into separate provable and practical exploration discussions, assumptions move into the main text, and the scaling-ablation discussion moves to Appendix E. Authorship text changes and acknowledgments and a limitations section are added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column format, redraws Figure 1, and removes v1's detailed CAE+ workflow Figure 2. Existing scaling plots are merged with DSAC plots in appendix Figure 4. Habitat trajectories, a results table, task-name mapping, and additional hyperparameter tables introduce substantial new displays.

improvement.justification: The Habitat evaluation adds useful evidence in a different reward regime and visual domain, while algorithm/proof corrections and expanded implementation documentation improve clarity and reproducibility. The gains are limited by continued reliance on unreported baseline results and only sketched handling of adaptive dependence and Thompson-sampling failure probabilities in Appendix D. The revision strengthens the paper without fully resolving its theoretical and comparative-evidence gaps.
